## Counting rule
A **canonical leaf** = one distinct Swift source call site (stable line range) that generates one semantically distinct visible object or one repeated-object family sharing geometry role, material role, and source location. A **rendered instance** = one `SCNNode` actually appended to the scene graph by that call site during a single execution of `buildScene()` (the entire environment + book stand + shop cabinet is built exactly once per `BookstoreSceneCoordinator` instance; category-selection only re-skins materials/textures on the same instances, it does not create or destroy nodes — verified by reading `updateShopSample`/`updateShopSelection`/`updateShopPresentation`, none of which call `addChildNode` on new geometry). Instance counts for `stride`/`0..<N`/array-literal loops are exact integer counts of the loop's iterations. For the four call sites that gate an extra node behind `Int.isMultiple(of:)` on a compound index (`addSideShelves` "band" and "stacked" accents, `addBackShelves` "band" accent), the exact instance count was derived by residue-class (mod-`n`) enumeration over the full iteration space and cross-checked with two independent derivations per site (both agreed); no code execution was available to verify this arithmetic mechanically, which is recorded as a limitation, not suppressed.
